critical_code_review_comments: server.py lines ~2192-2206 (per-row signal block) is clean: two-bucket logic is explicit, comments document WHY the field split was needed (production 92.4% inflation RCA), no fallback can re-introduce 100% inflation because the only branch that sets market_share_pct is gated on n_comp>=1 AND market_units_for_sku>0.

server.py line ~2247 market_coverage_pct uses len(pricing_rows)/total_count — correctly counts the 'has competitor pricing' set, not the more restrictive 'has share' set. This is the iter18→iter19 fix in one line.
server.py line ~2250 share_sample_size = len(share_rows) transparently surfaces the denominator of avg_market_share so a 0.0 reading over 49 products isn't misread as a 0.0 reading over 2081.

MyProductsPage.jsx line ~163 coverage accent flip: `(kpis.market_coverage_pct ?? 0) < 20 ? RED : GREEN` is a simple binary threshold — works for the current 37.2 vs 2.4 polarity but a 3-tier (red <10, yellow 10-30, green >30) would communicate data-quality progression better. Not blocking.
MyProductsPage.jsx line ~162 share sub-text correctly null-guards on `kpis.share_sample_size != null` so older clients without the new KPI field won't crash — good defensive coding.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter19 splits the Market Coverage KPI into two honest signals — coverage (774/2081=37.2%, 'do we have competitor pricing?') vs share-sample (49 rows, 'do we have BOTH a match AND velocity to compute share?'). Both backend and frontend confirmed end-to-end on preview. The kpi-kpi_market_share-sub testid is NEW in iter19 and renders 'across N products'. The retired has_market_data field MUST NOT come back. NOTE: as of this run the DataFreshnessBanner is now showing a RED 'Sync alarm: Last sync was 12.5h ago' because iter18's manual sync aged past 12h — this finally validates iter18's untested alarm→RED override path. If the next iteration triggers another sync, the banner will return to normal (yellow this_week bucket).
rca_of_the_issue: Iter18 conflated 'has at least one competitor match' (~774 products) with 'has BOTH match AND non-zero qty_sold_est' (~49 products) into a single has_market_data field, then used that single field for both the per-row market_share_pct gate AND the market_coverage_pct numerator. Result: market_coverage_pct came out as 49/2081=2.4% when the correct answer (matcher coverage of the catalogue) is 774/2081=37.2%. Iter19 splits into two booleans (has_competitor_pricing for coverage, has_market_share for the share ratio) so coverage and share-sample-size are independent metrics that can't drift again. Cross-page consistency test (per-row count == server-side aggregate) makes future definition drift caught by CI.
